User: Hello — I got your flyer about after-hours calls. We miss calls when we're out on jobs.
Agent: Got it — you saw our flyer about after-hours calls and missing calls when you’re out on jobs. What made you start looking to fix this right now?
User: We miss about 8 calls weekly, and I think 50% would book if someone answered.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—if you’re missing about 8 calls a week and half would book, that’s real revenue slipping away. When those calls come in and nobody picks up, what typically happens—do they leave a voicemail, text, or just move on?
User: They usually leave a voicemail.
Agent: Got it—so most of those missed calls end up as voicemails. When you get back to them, how often do you actually reach them versus they’ve already moved on?
User: When I call back, about half are still interested, but some have already moved on.
Agent: Mhm—so even when they leave a voicemail, you’re only saving about half and the rest have already moved on. What kind of business is this for you—what do you guys do?
User: We are a home remodeling and contractor company.
Agent: Got it—home remodeling and GC work, that makes total sense with you being out on sites. When those after-hours voicemails come in, are they mostly people trying to book an estimate, or more “quick question” shoppers?
User: Mostly people trying to book an estimate, rather than just quick questions.
Agent: Makes sense—those are the calls you really don’t want going to voicemail. When someone calls to book an estimate, what’s the usual next step you want them scheduled for (like an in-home visit, site check, or a quick phone consult)?
User: An in-home visit is usually the next step to provide a detailed estimate and consultation.
Agent: Got it—so the goal is getting them booked for that in-home visit and detailed estimate. If you had a way to capture those after-hours calls and lock in the visit right then, would you want it to book straight onto your calendar or just collect their info for you to confirm?
User: I would prefer it to collect their info for confirmation before booking onto the calendar.
Agent: Got it—so you’d want it to grab their details first, then you confirm before anything hits the calendar. Mind if I do a super quick 30‑second calculation on what those missed calls could be costing you?
User: Sure, go ahead. I'm curious to know how much those missed calls might be costing us.
Agent: Perfect—so we’ve got the first two numbers: about **8 missed calls a week**, and you figure **50%** would book if someone answered. What’s your average job value, ballpark (like $5k, $10k, $25k)?
User: Our average job value is around $2,500.
Agent: Got it — using your numbers (8 missed calls/week × 50% booking × $2,500 average job), that’s about **$10000 a week**… and that’s just one week — about **$43300 over a month**. Does that feel about right to you?
User: Yes, that sounds about right. It's a significant amount potentially lost from those missed calls.
Agent: Yeah… that’s exactly why this is worth fixing. It’s a 20‑minute walkthrough—Jay will show you how we capture those after‑hours estimate calls and collect the right info so you can confirm and book more of them. What’s better for you this week—later today or tomorrow?
User: Tomorrow works better. What times are available?
Agent: Got it—tomorrow works. Before I pull up times, what time zone are you in: Eastern, Central, Mountain, or Pacific?
User: We are in the Mountain time zone.
Agent: Perfect—Mountain time. What’s your first name?
User: I'm Susan.
Agent: Got it, Susan — and what’s your last name?
User: My last name is Park.
Agent: Thanks — and what’s the name of your company?
User: The name of my company is Cornerstone Remodeling.
Agent: Got it—Cornerstone Remodeling. And… is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you?
User: No, the best contact number is +13039150001.
Agent: Got it — so the best number is 303-915-0001. Just to confirm, did I get that right?
User: Yes, that's correct. The best number is 303-915-0001.
Agent: Perfect, thanks Susan. For tomorrow, I can get you in at **10:30 AM** or **11:15 AM** Mountain time — which works?
User: 10:30 AM Mountain time works for me. Book it.
Agent: Got it — so that’s **tomorrow (Aug 26) at 10:30 AM Mountain time**, correct?
User: Yes, book it. Tomorrow at 10:30 AM Mountain time works for me.
Agent: One moment while I confirm that.
Agent: Thanks—give me just a moment, I’m going to try that again on my side.
Agent: I’m having trouble getting the calendar to accept **tomorrow at 10:30 AM Mountain**—it’s showing a conflict on our end. What other time tomorrow would work for you?
User: Sure, I'll wait while you confirm that.
Agent: Thanks—so that slot is conflicting on our calendar right now. Would **11:15 AM Mountain tomorrow** work instead?
User: Yes, book it. 11:15 AM Mountain time tomorrow works for me.
Agent: One moment while I lock in 11:15 AM Mountain for tomorrow.
Agent: You’re booked for **Wednesday, Aug 26 at 11:15 AM Mountain time**. Before we wrap, can you re-share the best callback number in **+1##########** format?
User: Thank you, I'll be ready for the call at 11:15 AM Mountain time tomorrow.
Agent: Thanks, Susan! You’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details — you can add it to your calendar in one click, or reschedule if you need to. Is there anything else I can help you with? Really glad you called. Jay’s looking forward to it. Have a great day — bye!
